result.scope: Still air over a flat surface; steady glide polar of stuffed flying fish in a wind tunnel; ranges are upper bounds (every metre at (L/D)max). Only glide_range_lean_bound_m is covered by the Lean theorem glide_range_le. Launch speed is the organism's own sourced leap/burst speed (or a labelled what-if). Takeoff (taxiing), control, stability, flapping and burst power are not modelled. survives = null (a glide attempt is not a lethal perturbation in this model); feasible = lift can carry the weight at the reachable launch speed (null if no sourced launch speed). Out-of-validity results are reported under out_of_validity and are NOT law violations. STATE comes from the parametric body plan (anatomy-model/parametric), the project growth trajectories (development/) and physiology/ constants. Many inputs are assumed or borrowed from other species; check weakest_input on each field. MORPHOLOGICAL interpolation, not genetic hybridisation (anatomy-model/parametric/design-schema.json): a blended or edited parameter set is a shape, not an organism; it says nothing about whether such an animal could be bred, is viable, or is developmentally reachable.

entries.body: Genotype caveat for this edit. pectoral_area_over_SL2 is a morphology parameter: no causal chain in genotype/causal-chains.json maps any gene to a quantitative fin area, and gene-level edits are recorded-only in the studio (no model consumes them). The fin-size candidates closest to "a bigger pectoral fin" are kcnk5b (chain strength sufficiency, best link mechanism) and kcnh2a (chain strength sufficiency). For kcnk5b the chain breaks at molecular_function->process. Gaps include: "The clonal sufficiency experiments (transplantation, mosaic overexpression) were scored in caudal/dorsal fins and barbels, not in the pectoral fin." Dataset-wide constraint: "Every node below the pectoral fin is a zebrafish anatomy (ZFA) term, and every gene link is a zebrafish or medaka record. None of it is flying-fish data. A flying fish's wing is an enlarged pectoral fin." So approving this edit fixes a shape; it does not name a genotype that would produce it.
